device.name: TCD1304 linear CCD on a PSLab (open-spectrometer-python)

facts.text: The module is a TCD1304 linear CCD driver for Open Spectrometer; its pin map assigns master_clock to SQ1, sh_clock to SQ2, icg_clock to SQ3, +5V to PV1, GND to GND and OS to CH1
The module imports SerialHandler, Oscilloscope, PowerSupply and PWMGenerator from the external pslab SDK
TCD1304 is a linear CCD suitable for visible spectrum analysis
The class declares 3694 integration elements, a CH1 range constant of 4, a trigger voltage constant of 2 and two samples per element

The constructor accepts a device, an integration time defaulting to 10e-6 and a master clock frequency defaulting to 2e6; without a device it creates SerialHandler and composes the PWM generator, oscilloscope and power supply over it
Construction powers the CCD on and starts the SQ3, master and SH clocks
poweron sets the PV1 supply to 5 and poweroff sets it to 0
poweron is documented as turning the TCD1304 on and poweroff as turning it off
The ICG readout waits 3694 * integration_time seconds before the waveform is fetched
The oscillator frequency constant is 128e6 and the microseconds constant is 1e6
The master clock prescaler is derived from the oscillator frequency and the master clock frequency
The SH clock is generated at 1 / integration_time with a 50 percent duty cycle
read_signal selects the CH1 range and trigger, captures 3694 * 2 samples with a time gap of integration_time / 2 in microseconds, starts the ICG clock and returns the fetched waveform
The README describes the repository's main components as analyse.py and calibrate.py for webcam spectrometer images; it does not document the TCD1304 class
The README's calibration procedure assigns wavelength values to pixels by hand from a CFL reference; the TCD1304 class itself applies no wavelength calibration
